slides.title: Questions Chosen to Inform a Real Decision
bullets: Exploratory or reflective questions deliberately aimed at a decision the organisation needs to make
What separates a pleasant conversation from one that produces an actionable insight
Sets up the medical insight skills covered in full in Module 5

slides.title: A Good Conversation Isn't Automatically Useful
bullets: A technically excellent exploratory conversation can still produce nothing actionable
Real value connects to an evidence-generation priority, an unmet need, or a safety signal
Open dialogue alone does not guarantee organisational value

slides.title: Preparation Is Where Strategy Starts
bullets: Review what the current Medical Plan and evidence-generation agenda are trying to learn
Revisit open questions the last few visits with this expert left unresolved
Identify the therapy area's biggest current uncertainty
Design two or three strategic questions from that preparation

slides.title: Generic Warm-Up vs Strategic Question
bullets: A generic question like how do you approach this condition is fine as a warm-up, not strategic
A strategic version ties the same territory to a specific evidence-generation gap
Still genuinely open, with no predetermined right answer

slides.title: Strategic, Not Extractive
bullets: Strategic questions must stay balanced across visits
Too much transactional focus makes the relationship feel purely extractive
Weaving a few strategic questions into genuine curiosity marks a senior-level MSL skill

takeaway.title: Strategic questions turn open, curious conversation into insight the organisation can actually act on
bullets: Preparation before the visit is what makes a question strategic
Strategic questions stay genuinely open, not leading
Balance strategic intent with real curiosity so the relationship doesn't feel extractive
